src/domain/repositories.ts: `TaskFilter.status?: TaskStatus` reuses the type from task.ts instead of redefining the status values.
src/domain/repositories.ts: `ProjectRepository`, `UserRepository` and `TaskRepository` are ports typed against the module's own entities `Project`, `User` and `Task`.
src/domain/project.ts and src/domain/user.ts: `Project` and `User` are plain entities with an id and a name. They contain no logic from other concerns and don't repeat any rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The domain module passes. All four files cover one concern: the task-management domain model. That means the entities (Project, User, Task) plus the repository ports for them. Each rule is kept in one place. The status values are defined once, in `taskStatuses` / `TaskStatus` in task.ts. The "already done" check lives only in `Task.markDone`, which throws `TaskAlreadyDoneError`. repositories.ts uses the module's own types rather than redefining them. For example, `TaskFilter.status` uses the imported `TaskStatus` type instead of a separate string union. No file goes around the module's abstractions or contains unrelated code such as infrastructure or presentation logic. Project and User are thin data holders, but that doesn't break the module's cohesion.
